Traffic halted across key crossing just hours before Vladimir Putin meets Donald Trump and Xi Jinping

Ukraine struck the Kerch Bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea reportedly without using Elon Musk’s Starlink satellite network.

“For the first time in history, we used all these drones to pass video signals to missiles so they could hit precise points on the bridge. We showed we can conduct such operations without Starlink,” The Times quoted a Ukrainian military officer involved in the operation as saying.

“We planned this as a symbolic gesture before the meeting of Trump, Putin, and Xi, to show that Putin is weak,” he added.

The development comes amid tensions over SpaceX’s restrictions on Ukraine’s military satellite connectivity.

Meanwhile, traffic across the Crimean Bridge has been temporarily suspended following a third Ukrainian attack on the crossing this week, local authorities said.

Crimea’s Russian-installed governor Sergei Aksyonov said officials are assessing the damage to the strategic link connecting mainland Russia with the annexed peninsula – marking another humiliating blow for Vladimir Putin hours before he is set to meet Donald Trump and Xi Jinping for high-stakes nuclear talks in China.

The strike has deepened friction between Washington and its European allies ahead of Thursday’s Coalition of the Willing summit in Berlin.

US president Donald Trump said Washington and Beijing wanted to help end the war in Ukraine as he met Chinese president Xi Jinping ahead of a trilateral summit with Russian leader Vladimir Putin.

“We’re looking to both help with respect to the war with Russia and Ukraine. I’d like to see it ended, I think I can speak for both of us, very much,” Trump said.

Trump also held separate talks with Putin, calling him “my friend” and saying: “Wonderful things can come out of this – or at least start.”

Russian authorities have charged two people who donated to a 2023 fundraiser for political prisoners, alleging the money went to the banned Anti-Corruption Foundation of late opposition leader Alexei Navalny.

One donor has been fined, while the other fled Russia and faces up to eight years in prison.

Organisers of the fundraiser, run by exiled broadcaster Dozhd (TV Rain), deny any links to Navalny’s foundation and say the donations were intended solely to support political prisoners.

Australian prime minister Anthony Albanese used the Apec leaders’ meeting to tell Russian president Vladimir Putin to end the four-year war in Ukraine.

Addressing Putin directly, who was seen looking down during Albanese’s remarks in front of more than 20 world leaders, the Australian prime minister said: “Two of the biggest causes of disruption to trade are the conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East, and we must do all we can to end them.

“Conflict in the Middle East is having an impact on global inflation and causing cost of living pressures in our economies.

“And I say very directly to President Putin: end your war, end it now.”

Traffic was temporarily suspended on the Crimea bridge on Thursday following an attack, in the third such incident targeting the key crossing this week, according to The Moscow Times.

Sergei Aksyonov, the Russian-installed governor of Crimea announced the suspension in a post on Telegram, adding that authorities were assessing the damage caused by the attack.

The bridge connects mainland Russia with Crimea. It is a strategically important route for Russia, serving both civilian traffic and military logistics.

Wednesday night’s incident marks the third attack on the bridge this week, increasing pressure on one of Russia’s most important transport links to the peninsula.

The Pentagon’s top policy official Elbridge Colby criticised Ukraine’s long-range strikes on Russia during a tense meeting with European allies in Brussels, arguing they offered little military benefit.

The Telegraph reported that he then left before hearing Ukraine’s classified briefing on the effectiveness of the attacks.

According to a German source cited by the outlet, the incident alarmed European officials who accused the Trump administration of echoing Russia’s position.

Britain and Germany defended Ukraine’s strikes, saying they weaken Russia’s war machine and put pressure on Vladimir Putin.

The European Commission has proposed a €45bn loan to Ukraine for 2027 to help cover a looming funding shortfall and rising military costs as Russia intensifies its attacks.

The loan will be split between €25bn for military support and €20bn for civilian needs, including schools and hospitals.

European Commission president Ursula von der Leyen said: “We think this is the best way to give Ukraine a strong hand at the negotiating table. And Ukraine only needs to repay once Russia pays for the damage it has caused in Ukraine.”

However, four EU countries – Slovakia, Czechia, Hungary and Bulgaria – have said they will not participate. The EU is also seeking another €25bn from non-EU allies, including the UK, Norway and Canada, to help plug Ukraine’s estimated €70bn funding gap.

Britain has separately pledged 1,000 long-range attack drones as part of a £260m military aid package.

“The UK will do everything we can to ensure Ukraine is able to defend itself,” prime minister Andy Burnham said.

Prince Harry says he would rejoin the British Army to fight against Russia if needed, saying he believes Europe has finally “woken up to the threat” of Kremlin leader Vladimir Putin.

On a visit to Lviv in western Ukraine, the Duke of Sussex said he believed the UK and Russia had effectively been in conflict for the past decade.

“Just because there’s not drones, bullets and rockets flying at us, it doesn’t mean that we’re not at war,” he said.

The Duke said the UK could learn a lot from Ukraine’s resistance against Russian aggression, adding: “If asked to sign up again, if the need is there, then I will 100 per cent be there to serve my country alongside my fellow veterans and service personnel.”

“There is a lot that we can learn from Ukraine. I think there’s a lot that the whole world can learn from Ukraine,” he told The Telegraph.

Ukraine has confirmed that it struck two oil refineries in southern Russia overnight into Wednesday, targeting facilities that Kyiv says supply fuel to Russian forces fighting on the frontlines.

Ukraine’s general staff said yesterday that the strikes hit storage tanks at the Ilsky refinery and a processing unit at the Afipsky refinery, both located in Russia’s Krasnodar region.

The two facilities were also targeted on Sunday night.

According to the Ukrainian military, the refineries have a combined processing capacity of about 95m barrels of oil a year and supply Russian troops operating in southern and eastern Ukraine.
